answer: One concrete mechanism: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because cipher only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any opal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
